title: Ai Ore! Love Me!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Mizuki, a tall, boyish girl who is idolized as the 'prince' of her girls' school, leads the band Blaue Rosen and reluctantly lets Akira, a small, pretty boy known as the 'princess' of a boys' school, join as a member (Manga Bookshelf review). Their romance faces pressure from Mizuki's classmates and her school's student council because of the boys' school's bad reputation (VIZ blurb via AniList). This record is Mayu Shinjo's Asuka continuation of an earlier series (MangaUpdates).
life_message: It suggests that love can grow between people who do not fit expected gender roles (to verify).

content.note: Rescues from threatening suitors (review); MangaUpdates lists Prisoner/s and Sadist/s.
Mizuki's 'virtue is threatened' at a school trip (review).

Teen romance between high-school students with possessive love, stolen kisses and sexual tension (MangaUpdates Lust, Possessive Lover/s, Obsessive Love); rated Older Teen 16+ (review). No sex scene reported.
Mizuki's insecurity about her height and fear of men after a childhood crush (review).
Possessive, pushy romance; Akira poses as a girl to join a trip (review; MangaUpdates).
Live-action film adaptation (MangaUpdates); band and idol culture.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Couple resists student council and classmates' pressure (VIZ blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Band loyalty over school groups; family not central.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gender-flipped roles, though reviewer says stereotypes return.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Rock band, romance and self-image drive the story.

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese single-sex school culture, where students crown a 'prince' and 'princess', and shoujo conventions of the protective male lead.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer calls it predictable and stereotyped, not moralizing (Manga Bookshelf).
delivery.note: The gender-flip is played for romance and comedy rather than argued.

winners_losers: Akira and Mizuki's romance wins over classmates' disapproval; a reviewer notes traditional rescuer-and-rescued roles win out over the gender-bending setup.
to_verify: VIZ's English 'Ai Ore! Love Me!' run may combine this Asuka continuation with the earlier Shogakukan series; check volume mapping (ANN lists 8 volumes).
